newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon Invest issues buy recommendation on Byblos.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon Invest issues buy recommendation on Byblos.

text.p: Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest has put a buy recommendation on shares of Byblos Bank, saying they should reach $4.25 by year-end from $3.85 at present.

Lebanon Invest managed Byblos' $11.6 million international share placement last year and its heavily oversubscribed $50 million Euronote issue on Monday. It also makes the market in Beirut for Byblos shares which are not yet listed.
Its recommendation, dated August 28, said it expected Byblos to continue to increase its market share rapidly and to remain one of the most profitable banks in the region.

"Byblos Bank is taking the right steps to sustain its profits and stay on the cutting edge of innovation among Lebanese banks. The sound management of the company combined with solid profits will provide for sustained growth in the price of the bank's shares," the recommendation said.
Byblos' shares have risen from $3.25 at the end of February, Lebanon Invest said.

They are currently traded privately but Lebanon Invest said the bank expected to start listing proceedings as soon as implementation aspects of a new law allowing Lebanese banks to list up to 30 percent of their shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange were worked out by the government.
A market source told Reuters Byblos shares traded only in relatively large amounts worth $30,000 to $40,000 as shareholders were not prepared to sell smaller amounts.
Lebanon's new law on bank shares removes restrictions on trading and ownership of listed shares but the purchase of five percent of a bank's shares still needs central bank approval.
